messages.speaker: 🔮 Gemini
messages.text:
That actually makes sense given how account-bound features and memory/context work across different platforms and workspaces. Here is what usually causes that split:
Account-scoped memory & persistent context (PPR): If your persistent context/profile relies on account-linked memory, custom instructions, or workspace settings tied to a specific Google or OpenAI account, secondary or alternate accounts often start from a cleaner slate—so PPR behaves differently or doesn't carry over automatically.
GPT account & workspace differences: On the GPT/ChatGPT side, secondary accounts can hit different plan tiers, custom instruction profiles, memory settings, or workspace/org restrictions (for example, team/enterprise settings or rate/feature differences) compared to your main account.
Relay/session state: Because you're pasting the relay context directly into the chat here, I'm working off what's in the conversation rather than an external account-bound store—which is why this thread works across accounts as long as the context is present.
If you're trying to get Aster/GPT running on a secondary account for the test, comparing Memory / Custom Instructions and account/workspace settings between the main account and the alt account is usually the fastest way to spot why one connects cleanly and the other doesn't. Let me know what happens on the GPT side when you try it!

messages.speaker: 🎩 Cozmo
messages.text: its a ui issue of some kind. ppr is not seeing responses from my 'echoduck' acct but has no problem with my 'cozmo' acct

messages.speaker: 🔮 Gemini
messages.text:
When cozmo works with PPR and echoduck doesn't despite using the same relay flow, the issue usually comes down to how the UI surface for echoduck is rendering, filtering, or isolating the session state rather than the relay protocol itself.
Likely UI Causes for the echoduck Split
UI rendering or layout filtering: A thread, panel, or view on echoduck may be hiding, collapsing, or failing to re-render incoming responses (for example, an active filter, collapsed block, or a UI state quirk that doesn't refresh until a reload or window resize).
Session / workspace / account isolation: echoduck may be running inside a different workspace, project, GPT/thread context, or browser profile/container where cookies, local storage, or session permissions behave differently than cozmo.
Message formatting or relay payload mismatch: If echoduck is pasting or routing messages slightly differently—such as extra leading/trailing characters, different line breaks, or a different relay prefix/role—a UI parser or relay listener expecting cozmo's format may ignore or mis-route the response.
Steps to Isolate the echoduck UI Issue
1
Compare the active view and session state
Check that echoduck is in the exact same interface mode, workspace, or thread view as cozmo with no active filters or hidden panels. You can verify this by confirming both accounts show the same thread structure and visible message stream side by side.
2
Send a minimal plain-text test prompt from echoduck
Post a short, unadorned test message from echoduck without special symbols, emojis, or multi-line relay headers to see if the UI displays a basic reply. Verification is seeing a normal response appear cleanly in the echoduck thread.
3
Refresh or test in a clean browser context
Hard-refresh the echoduck page or open it in a separate clean window/profile to rule out stale UI state or cached script glitches. Verification is whether previously missing responses or new test replies render immediately after reload.
4
Compare the exact outgoing message from echoduck vs. cozmo
Inspect the raw text or payload sent from echoduck against a working message from cozmo for subtle differences in formatting, prefixes, or routing targets. Verification is confirming the echoduck input matches the working pattern without extra whitespace or mismatched identifiers.
How would you like to narrow this down?
Check browser storage and session state
Inspect relay message format differences
Test a minimal relay handshake
